A.notes: A has a clear developer-tool idea and a strong headline, and it does include a believable terminal/result demo. In the scroll strip, motion reads mainly as staged reveals and typed-in content rather than a stronger narrative device. Craft and accessibility are notably hurt by the measured contrast failures and the 375px horizontal overflow.

B.notes: B communicates faster by putting the install command and the working product directly in the hero, which fits the on-call engineer audience well. The scroll strip shows purposeful section-by-section reveals that support comprehension, and the reduced-motion fallback appears intact. It is still a familiar dark SaaS/developer aesthetic, but it is cleaner and more complete than A.

raw.why: B is better because it shows the product working sooner, is cleaner across desktop and mobile checks, and passes the hard gates that A fails.
